Call Patricia Hawkins (CEO) under the framing of a routine post-dinner follow-up — thank her for the gathering, ask if there are any strategic priorities she wants GMs to be watching or preparing for from the floor level. Listen for what she volunteers, what she avoids, and how she sounds.
past_actions.emotional_state: controlled unease — outwardly steady, inwardly shaken in a way he won't admit to anyone including himself

past_actions.summary: Request a private, one-on-one sit-down with Patricia Hawkins — not a phone call, an in-person meeting. Frame it as a GM operational briefing: floor plan financing concerns, staffing continuity, Q2 inventory strategy. But the real agenda is to get her to tell me, without a room full of people watching, what the actual plan is for this store. Is Regional Auto Group holding Millfield? Is there a timeline I need to know? I have 4 dependents and I am not going to manage this floor blind for another tick.
past_actions.emotional_state: Visibly composed. Doing his job. The unease is present but contained — he's leaning into the floor work because motion feels like control. Privately: more unsettled than tick 1, because 'rumor' no longer applies. What he felt last tick as a maybe is now a when.

past_actions.summary: Read Patricia's strategic analysis carefully and respond with a one-page GM floor memo that corroborates her modeling with real floor data: YTD traffic numbers, test-drive conversion rates, service lane utilization, and current inventory carrying costs. I want her to see that I understand the numbers, I am not in denial, and I am the most useful GM she has in this transition. I am not just reacting — I am showing her the floor-level signal that her spreadsheet cannot capture. This is how I secure my seat at the table.

Walk into Patricia's executive review with unfiltered 30-day floor data: actual foot traffic numbers (down 14% vs. prior 30 days), test-drive conversion rate (dropped from 31% to 22%), service lane utilization (holding at 79% — the one bright spot), and current inventory carrying cost per unit. No softening. No narrative spin. Just the numbers, annotated with what I believe is driving each trend. Then make a direct verbal case: service lane is the moat, not the showroom. If Regional Auto Group consolidates, consolidate around certified technicians and service capacity. I am the GM who can manage that transition without losing the techs.

Request an in-person sit-down with Patricia Hawkins in her new owner-operator capacity within the next 5 business days. The agenda is explicit: what is my role in the restructured organization, what authority do I retain over the Millfield location, and is there a formal Q2 operational plan she wants me to execute. I go in having already internalized the numbers — service lane at 79%, showroom down, conversion rates off — and I do not pretend any of this is recoverable without a deliberate pivot. I also raise the $12k stay bonus Jake mentioned: I want to know if that program exists, whether it applies to floor sales staff, and whether I have any role in administering it.

Update the three-tier asset map draft to incorporate the RoboRide pricing collapse as a structural accelerant. The $0.12/mile price point with 8-minute residential coverage fundamentally changes the timeline assumptions in section two of the assessment — the 18-to-24 month window I had projected for meaningful ownership attrition now compresses to 9-to-12 months at the outside. I revise the tier-one urgency language, update the showroom revenue projection downward, and add a new sub-section on what the delivery partnership means for fleet and commercial vehicle service demand — that is actually a potential upside for the service lane if we position for it. I push a revised draft to Patricia today with a one-paragraph cover note flagging the timeline compression.

Send Patricia a direct, brief message. Not a memo. Not a presentation. A single paragraph: I have delivered the asset map. The consolidation is executing on the timeline we discussed. I have not received a response to the compensation component I flagged when I submitted the final document. I am asking for a 30-minute call this week — not about operations, not about the floor — specifically about the consulting arrangement for the assessment work. I am not asking her to pay me for employment I no longer hold. I am asking her to acknowledge that the work I did over the last several ticks was contracted deliverable work that has real value, and that she commit to either compensating it or declining explicitly so I can close that account and move forward. I am not going to let this drift into ambiguity. The ask is specific, the timeline is this week.
past_actions.emotional_state: Controlled and sober. The anger phase has not passed — it is still there, underneath — but it has quieted into something more functional. I built the case for this consolidation. I did the work. I did not get a response to my compensation ask. That is not grief anymore. That is a business problem and I know how to work business problems. What I am feeling most sharply right now is the distance between the identity I have carried for 32 years and the reality of what the next chapter looks like. I am not a GM right now. I am a consultant who has not been paid. That is a different thing to be. I am adjusting to it in real time.

past_actions.summary: Respond to Patricia's consulting contract offer in writing — send a brief confirmation acknowledging the $4,500/month 90-day engagement, the scope (assessment finalization and transition-phase operational advisory), and the expectation of a signed document from her side. If she has already sent the signed contract, acknowledge receipt and confirm commencement. This closes the ambiguity that has been the central unresolved thread since tick 8. The contract is the single most important operational item this tick.

reflections.reflection: Six months in and the shape of what is happening is no longer deniable. The showroom is down 14% in foot traffic, test-drive conversion has dropped nearly 10 points, and the only thing holding at anything like normal is the service lane at 79%. I have been doing the right things — calling Patricia early, presenting real numbers, making the case for the service lane as the moat. But Patricia is now an owner-operator instead of a corporate CEO, which means the structure I was navigating has changed underneath me. I do not know exactly what my role is in the new organization. That is the thing I need to resolve in the next two weeks.
reflections.identity_shift: I have always defined myself by this floor. Thirty-two years in automotive retail, GM for nine of them. That identity is still intact but it is under pressure in a way it has never been before. The skills I have — managing people, reading buyers, keeping a service lane running — those still matter, but skill_relevance at 0.25 tells me the world is not going to keep paying for them at the rate it has. I am starting to think of myself less as 'car guy' and more as 'transition manager.' I am not sure I like that but I am not resisting it the way I would have a year ago.
regrets: Did not get explicit confirmation from Patricia that my service lane pivot argument landed before she restructured. I made the case but I do not know if it registered.
Waited too long to ask directly about the $12k stay bonus program. I heard about it secondhand through Jake. That kind of information should not be reaching me through the floor.
Tick 3 I went routine. With a 10-month runway and four dependents, routine was a mistake. Every tick costs me information and position.
successes: Presented unfiltered floor data to Patricia in tick 5 — no spin, no narrative management, just numbers. That was the right call and it was hard to do.
Maintained trust with Jake Morrison and Angela Wright. Both of them are treating me as someone worth engaging honestly, which means I have not lost credibility on the floor.
Savings are still at roughly $86,900 after a rough two ticks. The runway is real. I have time to make smart decisions if I move now.
reflections.adaptation_notes: I am adapting, but slowly and reactively rather than proactively. Each tick I respond to what Patricia does rather than shaping the situation. That is partly my position — I am power-under her — but it is also a character pattern. I defer, I gather data, I present it cleanly. That is valuable but it is not enough in a restructuring. I need to start making asks, not just presentations. The meeting with Patricia this tick has to be a genuine negotiation about my role and authority, not another briefing where I hand her information and wait to see what she does with it.

reflections_tick9.reflection: The consolidation I designed is now executing. One location closes by end of Q2. I provided Patricia with the asset map, the service lane analysis, the revised timeline projections — all of it. The work landed. She moved on it within 72 hours. And I am unemployed, watching it happen from outside the organization I spent nine years inside. The most significant open thread is the compensation demand I attached to the final deliverable at tick 8. Patricia has not responded. Her inbox this tick is all operational execution — coordinating Angela's transition program, reaching out to Tamika, running the clock on the closure announcement. No acknowledgment of my ask. That silence after delivery of the promised document is the defining data point of this tick. I have stopped performing patience and started treating this as a negotiation I have not yet closed.
reflections_tick9.identity_shift: The 'car guy' identity that has been under pressure since tick 1 is now functionally retired. I am not managing a floor. I am not directing staff. I am a contractor whose final deliverable has been accepted and whose invoice has not been paid. That is a different kind of person than I have ever had to be. The shift is uncomfortable but it is also clarifying — I know what I am worth because I just watched Patricia use what I produced to make a million-dollar operational decision in 72 hours. Thirty-two years of floor experience translated into exactly that kind of analysis. The question now is whether I accept that value only in retrospect or start asking for it prospectively. I am choosing the latter.
regrets: Did not get the compensation arrangement in writing before delivering the final asset map. Verbal commitment in a restructuring is worth nothing — I learned this in 2008 and let myself forget it because the relationship felt solid.
Spent too many ticks making presentations instead of making asks. Patricia respected the data I brought. She would have respected explicit asks sooner if I had made them.
Did not build a parallel track job search until unemployment was already a reality. Should have opened those conversations quietly at tick 6 when the restructuring shape became clear.
successes: Delivered the revised asset map on the 72-hour deadline with the RoboRide pricing collapse fully integrated. The analysis was the right level of honest — Patricia acted on it immediately. That is the outcome I wanted.
Attaching the compensation demand to the deliverable at tick 8 was the first genuinely self-directed move I have made. It was the right move regardless of outcome. I named my price.

Maintained functional relationships with Angela Wright, Jake Morrison, and the service lane staff through the restructuring. These people are still talking to me honestly. That is a real asset in a sector where trust collapses fast.
reflections_tick9.adaptation_notes: The pattern I am trying to break is reactive positioning — waiting for Patricia's move, then responding to it with data. That pattern produced good work and insufficient compensation. The pattern I need to build is: identify leverage, name it explicitly, hold it until the other party responds. The compensation ask was step one of that new pattern. The next step is opening a parallel job search not as a fallback but as a genuine market test of what my skills are worth outside this particular power structure. The sector is contracting. My skills have a window. I need to use it while the window is open.
